text: Understanding Git branching is an important skill for modern software development. A branch lets you work on new features without affecting the main code. Developers often create feature branches to experiment safely and keep their work organized. When the work is finished, merging brings the changes back into the main branch. Pull requests allow team members to review code before it is merged, which improves quality and teamwork. This version control workflow helps teams collaborate smoothly and avoid conflicts. By using branches, merges, and pull requests together, developers can manage projects more efficiently and keep the codebase stable and reliable.
